readings: Join each lab test to its patient and compute the CPK ÷ GPT ratio per test, ignoring tests where the ratio is missing. Average the ratio separately for every distinct `SEX` value. Patients whose `SEX` is an empty string '' or missing are dropped first, so only real sex values form groups. Take the plain mean of all these group averages and keep the groups whose average is above it. Then take the mean of the kept groups' averages and keep the groups above that second mean. Return one unrounded row with: the average of the remaining groups' ratio averages, the average amount by which they exceed the first mean, and the average amount by which they exceed the second mean.
queries:
WITH ratios AS (
    SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, CAST(l.CPK AS REAL) / l.GPT AS ratio
    FROM Laboratory l
    JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID
    WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND p.SEX <> ''
),
grp AS (
    SELECT SEX, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio
    FROM ratios
    WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY SEX
),
m1 AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean1 FROM grp
),
kept1 AS (
    SELECT g.SEX, g.avg_ratio
    FROM grp g, m1
    WHERE g.avg_ratio > m1.mean1
),
m2 AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean2 FROM kept1
),
kept2 AS (
    SELECT k.SEX, k.avg_ratio
    FROM kept1 k, m2
    WHERE k.avg_ratio > m2.mean2
)
SELECT AVG(k.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_remaining,
       AVG(k.avg_ratio - m1.mean1) AS avg_excess_over_first_mean,
       AVG(k.avg_ratio - m2.mean2) AS avg_excess_over_second_mean
FROM kept2 k, m1, m2;
